overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Blood That Carries the Soul, and the Guilt Offering of Doubt
overview.subtitle: Keritot 22a–22b
overview.hebrewSource: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְחַיֵּיב עַל סְפֵק מְעִילָה אָשָׁם תָּלוּי, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִים
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf pins down exactly which blood counts as 'blood with which the soul departs' — the blood whose consumption carries karet — through a dispute between Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish over whether only forcefully spurting blood qualifies, or also the very first red drops after the initial black ones. A rejected a fortiori argument about human milk, and Rav Sheshet's ruling on human blood, round out the chapter's treatment of blood's outer boundaries. The daf then turns to a new mishna launching a fresh debate: does uncertainty about misusing consecrated property (me'ila) require a provisional guilt offering, the way uncertainty about a sin-offering-level transgression does? Rabbi Akiva says yes; the Rabbis say no — and the Gemara traces their dispute to competing readings of a single connecting vav and a contested verbal analogy. The daf closes with two further mishnayot applying the same 'same species covers both certain and uncertain cases' principle to a woman's bird offering and to pieces of non-sacred and consecrated meat.

slides.title: 💉 Which Blood Carries the Soul?
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish define the boundary of karet-bearing slaughter blood

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rabbi Yoḥanan: only blood that spurts forcefully (מְקַלֵּחַ) counts as 'the blood with which the soul departs' — everything before or after is merely exudate
2️⃣ Reish Lakish: the boundary starts earlier — from the last BLACK drop onward, even before forceful spurting begins

3️⃣ Multiple baraitot seem to refute Reish Lakish (defining it strictly as 'while spurting'), but the Gemara reconciles them: they exclude only the black blood itself, not the first/last red drops, which still count even if merely flowing
4️⃣ A further baraita appears to refute him again — resolved as reflecting a genuine tannaitic dispute: Rabbi Elazar agrees with Rabbi Yoḥanan's position, Rabbi Shimon with Reish Lakish's

callout.label: Practical stakes:
callout.text: Rabbi Yirmeya's dilemma about blood collected in two separate cups (first cup: forceful spurt; second cup: mere flow) directly maps onto this dispute — Reish Lakish would obligate two sin offerings, Rabbi Yoḥanan only one.

slides.title: 🥛 Why Human Milk (and Blood) Escape the Prohibition
slides.subtitle: A rejected a fortiori argument, corrected by the Torah's own wording
rows: Non-kosher animals are LENIENT regarding contact-impurity but STRICT regarding their milk (forbidden) — so humans, who are STRICT regarding contact-impurity, should be even more STRICT regarding their milk
'And these are they which are impure to you' (Lev. 11:29) — 'these' (the specified non-kosher animals) are impure; human milk is not impure, but pure/permitted
One might still think blood — unlike milk, forbidden even from kosher animals — should apply to humans too; the same verse excludes human blood as well
Human blood carries not even a preference to abstain from it ab initio — the exclusion is complete

callout.label: Why the a fortiori fails:
callout.text: Intuitive logical inferences about severity can be overridden by the Torah's own explicit classification — 'these are impure' draws a hard boundary no inference can cross.

slides.title: ⚖️ Uncertain Misuse — Does It Need a Guilt Offering?
slides.subtitle: A new mishna: does the provisional guilt offering (for sin-offering-level doubt) extend to misuse of consecrated property?

lines.speaker: Rabbi Akiva
lines.text: Yes — one who is uncertain whether he misused consecrated property still brings a provisional guilt offering, just like ordinary uncertain sins.

lines.speaker: The Rabbis
lines.text: No — a provisional guilt offering applies only to uncertainty about SIN-OFFERING-level transgressions, not misuse.

lines.speaker: Rabbi Tarfon's proposal
lines.text: Why bring two separate guilt offerings ever? Bring the misuse payment plus a two-sela guilt offering, and STIPULATE: 'if certain, this is my definite guilt offering; if uncertain, the money is a donation and this animal is my provisional offering.'

lines.speaker: Rabbi Akiva's limit
lines.text: That works for SMALL amounts of misuse. But if the uncertain misuse involves 10,000 dinars, isn't it better to bring just the cheap provisional offering now, rather than pay the full massive sum on mere uncertainty?

lines.speaker: Resolution
lines.text: Rabbi Akiva concedes to Rabbi Tarfon's method specifically for minor cases of misuse.

callout.label: Underlying agreement:
callout.text: Both tanna'im accept that a certain guilt offering does not require prior knowledge from the very outset — it suffices that certainty eventually arrives.

slides.title: 🔗 Vav, Gezeirah Shava, and Juxtaposition
slides.subtitle: Tracing the Akiva/Rabbis dispute to its exegetical roots

nodes.content: 📜 The provisional-guilt-offering verse (Lev. 5:17) begins with 'AND if anyone sin' — does this vav connect it backward to the misuse passage, teaching that misuse too gets a provisional offering?
🔀 Rav Pappa clarifies: everyone agrees a vav CAN teach 'earlier from later' (proven elsewhere, e.g. northern slaughter for sheep from cattle) — so that's not the real dispute

🧩 The REAL dispute: a separate verbal analogy ('mitzvot'/'mitzvot') links the provisional guilt offering to the ordinary SIN offering — which requires karet for intentional violation. Since intentional misuse carries no karet (only death-at-Heaven's-hand or lashes), the Rabbis conclude misuse is EXCLUDED

⚖️ Rabbi Akiva rejects using that same analogy to also fix the OFFERING'S MINIMUM VALUE (2 shekels) — deriving that instead from 'this is the law of the guilt offering' (one law for all guilt offerings) — freeing him to read the vav literally and include misuse after all

callout.label: The elegant symmetry:
callout.text: Each sage uses ONE derivation (the vav, or the gezeirah shava) for one purpose and the OTHER derivation for the other — precisely reversed between Rabbi Akiva and the Rabbis.

slides.title: 🐦 Definite After the Fact
slides.subtitle: Two closing mishnayot apply 'one species covers both certain and uncertain' to new cases
rows: Woman's bird sin offering (uncertain miscarriage), certainty arrives before the bird is slaughtered
Convert it to a definite offering — same species covers both cases
Piece of non-sacred meat and piece of consecrated meat; ate one, doesn't know which
Exempt from a definite guilt offering; Rabbi Akiva obligates a provisional one
Then he ate the SECOND piece too
Now brings a definite guilt offering — he's certainly eaten the consecrated piece
Two different people each ate one piece
Rabbi Akiva: each brings his own provisional guilt offering. Rabbi Shimon: both bring ONE definite guilt offering together, as partners

callout.label: Setting up the next debate:
callout.text: Rabbi Yosei's view on the two-people scenario is cut off mid-sentence at the end of the daf — continuing directly into the next daf's analysis.

summary.principle: The precise blood that carries karet, and the precise scope of the provisional guilt offering, are both defined through careful textual analysis — distinguishing forceful spurting from mere flow, and tracing a single connecting letter and a contested verbal analogy to their furthest logical implications.

flowSteps.content: 💉 Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish define the karet-bearing blood of slaughter differently, reconciled through tannaitic sources
🥛 A tempting a fortiori about human milk and blood is overridden by the Torah's explicit classification
⚖️ Rabbi Akiva and the Rabbis dispute whether uncertain misuse of consecrated property requires a provisional guilt offering

columns.content: 🔗 Their dispute traces to competing uses of a connecting vav and a verbal analogy
🐦 Closing mishnayot extend the 'same species' principle to bird offerings and shared meat pieces

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: even a single conjunction or a shared phrase between two verses can determine an entire category's boundaries

quiz.q: According to Reish Lakish, when does the karet-bearing 'blood with which the soul departs' begin during slaughter?
o: Only once the blood spurts forcefully
From the last black drop onward, even before the blood begins spurting forcefully
Only after the animal is completely dead
Only from blood collected in a vessel
quiz.e: Reish Lakish holds the karet-bearing blood begins from the last black drop onward — earlier than Rabbi Yoḥanan's view, which requires forceful spurting.

quiz.q: According to the Gemara's resolution of the rejected a fortiori argument, why is human milk not forbidden despite the seemingly compelling logic that humans (strict on contact-impurity) should also be strict about their milk?
o: Because human milk is never produced
Because the verse 'these are they which are impure to you' (Leviticus 11:29) specifically classifies only the enumerated animals as impure, excluding human milk from the comparison
Because milk is never forbidden under any circumstances
Because the a fortiori argument was never actually proposed
quiz.e: The Torah's explicit classification in Leviticus 11:29 overrides the logical inference, establishing that only the specified non-kosher animals' milk (and blood) are forbidden, not humans'.

quiz.q: According to the mishna, what is Rabbi Akiva's position on whether uncertain misuse of consecrated property requires a provisional guilt offering?
o: He holds it never requires any offering
He holds it does require a provisional guilt offering, just as ordinary uncertain sin-offering-level transgressions do
He holds it always requires a definite guilt offering immediately
He agrees entirely with the Rabbis that no offering is needed
quiz.e: Rabbi Akiva rules that even uncertainty about misuse of consecrated property obligates a provisional guilt offering, disagreeing with the Rabbis who exempt such uncertainty entirely.

quiz.q: According to the Gemara, what is the actual basis of the Rabbis' exemption of uncertain misuse from a provisional guilt offering?
o: A simple rejection of Rabbi Akiva's authority

A verbal analogy ('mitzvot'/'mitzvot') linking the provisional guilt offering to the sin offering, which requires the underlying transgression to carry karet for intentional violation — something misuse of consecrated property lacks
The fact that misuse offerings are always more expensive
A general rule that guilt offerings are never brought for uncertainty
quiz.e: The Rabbis derive via a verbal analogy that the provisional guilt offering parallels the sin offering, which requires the underlying sin to carry karet when intentional; since intentional misuse carries no karet, misuse is excluded from the provisional guilt offering's scope.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Tarfon's proposed stipulation for uncertain misuse, what does the person say when bringing his combined offering?
o: That he refuses to bring any offering at all
That if it is certain he misused property, this is his definite payment and guilt offering; if uncertain, the money is a donation and the offering is provisional
That the priest must decide the offering's status
That he will wait until Yom Kippur to bring any offering
quiz.e: Rabbi Tarfon's stipulation allows one offering and payment to serve both possible outcomes, avoiding the need for two separate offerings by making the offering's status conditional on whether the misuse turns out to be certain or remains uncertain.
